cells.tense: You are moving from what you feel, and the direction holds because of that.
cells.ask: Take the next small step today without waiting to see past it. Let what you feel point the way; the walking is the part you supply.
cells.core:
You're headed somewhere, and the direction comes from real engagement rather than force. It doesn't feel like pushing — it feels like going. Feeling and motion are pointed the same way, so the next step is available even while the road ahead stays foggy.

That's the balance here: not seeing the whole route, and not needing to. You move, the way becomes a little clearer, you move again. Keep it lit that way. Doubt isn't a signal to demand the whole map before the next step; it's a signal to look at the step itself, take it, and let the fog thin where you've walked.
cells.sheetLine: You move because you feel it, and that's what makes it hold.
cells.verb: moving steadily toward a destination already chosen
cells.place: where the next step shows itself but the whole road doesn't

cells.tense: You are driving hard toward a future you have not arrived at, and the pace will not let up.
cells.ask: Before the next move, name what pace this needs. Then set one thing down — a task, a thread, a start — and leave it for a day.
cells.core:
The momentum has gotten ahead of the destination. You're already into the next thing before the current one has landed, bracing against an outcome you can't quite picture, and every step forward just reveals more to chase. What began as aim has become speed you're no longer steering.

When this is steady, you still move, and the pace matches the ground under you. You feel what's beneath before lifting the next foot. Ease isn't the opposite of drive; losing contact with the road is. Take one thing at the pace it deserves and notice what settles down with it — the road comes back into view when the feet stay on it.
cells.sheetLine: You're moving faster than the destination can keep up with.
cells.verb: moving steadily toward a destination already chosen

cells.tense: You felt something once that pointed forward, and you have been standing at that door long past it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing that's already over and put it down for good today. Clear a drawer, close a thread, tell someone it's finished. Let the room stay bare a week.
cells.core:
There's somewhere to go — that hasn't disappeared. What stopped is the walking. The feeling is there, the motion isn't, and the space between them has widened into a place to stand still in. Something ahead got asked to wait, and the waiting became where you live.

When this is steady, the feeling leads to a step and the step is enough. You don't need the ending to move. What's blocking that isn't more effort or more feeling — it's a thing that needs to be finished so the next step has somewhere to land. Finish it. That's the move, not a bigger push.
cells.sheetLine: You're still at a door that already shut behind you.

cells.tense: You are already moving, and you describe it as though it were happening to you.
cells.ask: Say out loud to one person what one ongoing effort is moving toward. If you can't say it, that tells you what to clear.
cells.core:
There's real momentum in how you spend your days — what you keep returning to, what you keep working at when stopping would be easier. That's yours. But describing it, the verbs go passive: it got busy, this ended up here, it's going where it goes. The steering is happening. You're just not claiming it.

When this is steady, you know what the motion is for and you say so, which locks nothing in place. Naming it lets you choose it, adjust it, or drop it on purpose — instead of finding out later you were headed somewhere you didn't pick. The work is already underway. Saying where it's pointed is the piece still missing.
cells.sheetLine: You're already moving. You just haven't claimed the steering.
cells.verb: moving steadily toward a destination already chosen
